trace.code: MethodPart::evaluate resolves the method descriptor and then goes straight to func.invoke / func.invoke_async — no check_allowed_function() on the resolved function name (unlike expr/function.rs:90, physical_expr/function/builtin.rs:46 and fnc/mod.rs:671)
fixed in 3.3.1: after descriptor.resolve(), insert ctx.check_allowed_function(func.name())?;
planning-time registry.get_method() resolves the descriptor with the same unchecked path

preconditions: operator hardens the deployment with --deny-funcs (or SURREAL_CAPS_DENY_FUNC) to forbid a function family such as array::*, file::*, http::*
an authenticated (or guest, when --allow-guests is set) subject that can submit a SurrealQL query over HTTP/WS/RPC

evidence.observed_result: v3.3.0 with --deny-funcs array::map: normal form 'RETURN array::map([1,2], |$x| $x*2)' -> ERR 'Function array::map is not allowed to be executed'; method form 'RETURN [1,2].map(|$x| $x*2)' -> {"result":[2,4],"status":"OK"} (BYPASS). v3.3.1: the same method form -> ERR NotAllowed (deny enforced). The fix adds ctx.check_allowed_function(func.name())?; after descriptor.resolve() in MethodPart::evaluate.
